references.text: Joseph promises to support his father, his brothers, and his entire father's household during the five remaining years of famine.
Pharaoh invites Joseph's family to Egypt and offers them the best the land has to offer, laying the foundation for Joseph's provision for the family.
Joseph assures his brothers that he will care for them and their children, demonstrating his ongoing concern for the family.
Joseph presents his father Jacob to Pharaoh after the family settles in Goshen, setting the context for the provision that follows.
Paul emphasizes the duty to provide for one's own, especially members of one's household, a principle Joseph lived out when he supported his entire father's household.
Luke confirms the historical and theological context of Joseph's care for the whole family as the foundation for Israel's growth in Egypt.
Shows the transition from personal trials with the brothers to the systematic provision for the entire family.
Highlights the connection between Joseph's public role as savior of the nation and his private responsibility toward his own family.
Demonstrates how Joseph's authority as ruler over the land was used concretely to save his own family.
Contrasts Joseph's role as a passive recipient of blessing in Potiphar's house with his active role as provider for his family.
